pages.title: What is AWS Lambda?
pages.content:
# AWS Lambda

AWS Lambda is a compute service that lets you run code without provisioning or managing servers.

## Event-driven execution

Lambda functions are invoked by events from many AWS services, including S3, EventBridge, API Gateway, and DynamoDB Streams.

## Scaling model

Lambda automatically scales by running code in response to each trigger. Concurrency controls and reserved capacity can be configured for predictable throughput.

## Operational guidance

Use structured logging and metrics to monitor function health. Set explicit timeouts and memory settings to balance latency and cost.

pages.title: Configure timeout for Lambda functions
pages.content:
# Configure timeout for Lambda functions

The timeout setting determines how long Lambda allows a function to run before stopping it.

## Why timeouts matter

Timeouts prevent runaway executions and protect downstream systems. Choose values based on expected payload size, external calls, and retriable failure patterns.

## Steps

1. Open the Lambda function configuration page.
2. Update Timeout under General configuration.
3. Deploy and validate with representative load tests.

## Troubleshooting

If timeout errors increase, profile cold starts, network calls, and dependencies. Consider increasing memory size to improve CPU allocation.

pages.title: Troubleshoot Lambda@Edge logs
pages.content:
# Troubleshoot Lambda@Edge logs

Lambda@Edge writes logs to CloudWatch in us-east-1. When debugging a regional request, check the CloudFront distribution behavior and associated function version.
